controls_available: Drag an unused pictured roll or chip card with the mouse onto one of the four compass directions and release to deliver a stroke.
Click CERTIFY SUNKEN BALL with the mouse to submit the transcript; certification is administrative.
Compass-button clicks are present but, in full mode, only display the drag instruction; no keyboard handler changes the puzzle.
autonomous_processes: None affecting task outcome: after initial render and between stroke releases, the generated course, hand, ball, and used-card set have no clock-driven or autonomous update.
Hover and drag CSS transitions may change presentation, but they do not change task state, legal moves, or action value.
grouped_control_modes: D = full-mode card_drag_to_compass stroke delivery, grouped across every unused-card/current-position occurrence for this difficulty and all seeds or attempts; certify_button is administrative and excluded.

clause_i.reason: For the grouped full-drag mode, an observation-free q cannot choose an optimal first card and direction across the generated instances: the generator applies a seed-dependent board reflection and direction transform and shuffles the visible hand, while I_t is identical before any action. This is static visual dependence, not a real-time process.

clause_ii.reason: With the configured w bound of 0 ms, one current screenshot exposes the static isometric course, surfaces, elevations, cup, ball, and dealt card types/distances. A screenshot-only policy can derive the next legal card/direction from that frame and repeat after each action; no chronological frame sequence is needed.

clause_iii.reason: There is no H_t to H_t^tau autonomous task-state evolution for any positive delay. The ball and used-card set change only synchronously in dispatch after pointerup, and certification only posts the already-built transcript. The CSS transition is presentation-only, so no outcome-affecting action becomes unavailable or strictly less effective during a no-action interval.

common_visible_process: None. The visible course and hand are static after generation; the only visible changes are action-caused ball/card updates and presentation-only hover/drag styling, so no common autonomous process can witness clauses (i)-(iii).

pre_run.reason: The mathematical definition already fails clause (iii), so the pre-run threshold cannot change the configuration-level label and was not needed.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 5 is the nine-stroke, 12-by-9 profile; full interaction is a direct card drag onto a compass direction; observation_window_ms is 0 and frames_per_observation is 1.
The exact difficulty-5 profile contains a fixed nine-card action plan and fixed counts for sand, water, ramps, decoys, and chip clearance.
Generation consumes the supplied control condition and creates the course from a deterministic seed-local RNG, with no runtime clock or evolving state.
The route tiles and cards are constructed synchronously from the fixed plan, and the solution is recorded as card/direction pairs.
Decoy tiles, reflection-transformed coordinates/directions, and shuffled card presentation vary the static visible instance; no later process mutates them.
Full-mode pointerdown/pointerup handles a card drag, and dispatch synchronously validates the transition, appends the event, updates the ball and used-card set, and redraws.
Certification posts the accumulated transcript; direct compass clicks are explicitly non-operative in full mode.
Rendering initializes the ball at the static course start and installs the hand, compass, canvas, and certification controls; the mechanic has no timer, interval, or animation-loop registration.
The only timing-related styling is a short card hover/drag transition and submit/hover presentation; it does not implement task-state motion.
The grader independently replays the submitted stroke events from the static start state, enforcing card legality, surfaces, heights, and exact card use before certification.
Grading checks the interaction-specific input source and the synchronously replayed final state; it has no elapsed-time or deadline condition.
The task verifier only loads the exported result and invokes the Cloudstep Caddie grader.
The normal scripted interaction performs every solution stroke before the administrative certification; its 120 ms waits do not invoke any task transition.
